atlas-cuaca/.title: Indonesian Weather Atlas · Klimatikal
atlas-cuaca/.description: A catalogue of weather and climate phenomena across Indonesia, from well documented to rarely recorded, local and regional. Each phenomenon has its own page: the name, the scientific explanation, local knowledge and where it occurs.

atlas-cuaca/angin-bahorok/.description: The Bahorok wind is a warm, dry downslope wind (the foehn effect) on the eastern side of the Bukit Barisan range in North Sumatra, blowing on the plains of Deli, Langkat and Serdang.

atlas-cuaca/borneo-vortex/.description: The Borneo vortex is a cyclonic circulation (turning counter-clockwise in the northern hemisphere) in the lower atmosphere around Borneo and the equatorial South China Sea.

atlas-cuaca/cens/.description: A low-level northerly flow that occasionally crosses the equator from the South China Sea into the Java Sea in northern-hemisphere winter, linked to heavy rain over Java and nearby areas.

atlas-cuaca/embun-upas/.description: A thin layer of ice that covers grass and crops on the Dieng Plateau on clear, cold dry-season nights; residents call it “poison dew” because it can kill potato plants.

atlas-cuaca/kabut-bromo/.description: Fog that blankets the Mount Bromo area and the Tengger caldera almost every morning and afternoon, limiting visibility for visitors.

atlas-cuaca/musim-bediding/.description: Bediding (a Javanese word) names a sharp temperature swing at the start of the dry season in Java and other places south of the equator: nights and early mornings turn very cold while daytime stays hot.
